principle: A watch is generated from continuous operational coverage, crew availability and ship policy. Class/era constrain the solution but do not hard-code one universal roster.

three_shift.canon_basis: Three shifts are directly supported aboard Enterprise-D and late-23rd-century/24th-century Starfleet practice.
three_shift.note: Ratios assign primary watch teams; active headcount at a moment also includes day staff, projects, maintenance and call-outs.

four_shift.canon_basis: Enterprise-D could be ordered from three to four shifts; the change created personnel scheduling problems.
four_shift.note: Used when command policy, fatigue management, mission tempo or staffing model justifies it; not automatically better.

calculation_rules: Do not divide total population by number of watches.
Remove civilians/passengers/non-duty residents before duty-roster calculation.
Create continuous station slots first, then assign one qualified primary and valid relief coverage per watch.
Add roaming/security/maintenance/medical coverage required by class, mission and readiness.
Add day staff separately; day staff can belong to a watch for recall purposes without occupying a continuous station.
Reserve/relief personnel remain real assigned crew and may be scheduled for training, maintenance or off-watch obligations.
Vacancies remain vacancies; generator may not spawn extra crew at runtime to hide shortages.
One character cannot satisfy overlapping incompatible assignments.
Alert states may call off-watch personnel to battle/emergency stations and create fatigue debt.
Watch handoff consumes time and transfers known unresolved state only.
Exact start/end times are stored on the individual ship schedule, not the class.

handoff_default_guidance.rule: Overlap must be scheduled and consumes time; emergencies may abbreviate it.

ai_boundary: AI cannot place an off-duty character on watch without assignment/recall state.
AI cannot invent a relief officer to cover a vacancy.
AI cannot alter shift length or pattern without command/order/state.
